sector_model: upstream oil and gas producer (largest US natural gas producer): production, realized price, hedging, adjusted EBITDAX, net debt, capex, reserves; GAAP net income distorted by derivative gains, so adjusted net income and cash flow used; generic P/E is commodity cycle dependent
thesis: Expand Energy produced 7.54 Bcfe/d in Q3 2026 (92% gas) and 9M operating cash flow was 4,675M against cash capex 2,298M, giving free cash flow of 2,377M as the company defines it (adjusted 2,401M). Net debt is 4,656M, 0.8x trailing adjusted EBITDAX of 5,805M. At 84.60 (2026-11-06) and 230.96M shares market cap is about 19.54B, enterprise value about 24.2B or 4.2x trailing adjusted EBITDAX, and 9M adjusted net income of 1,578M (6.66 per share) annualizes to about 8.88 per share or about 9.5x. It returned about 1.3B in nine months (900M buybacks, 411M dividends) after funding the 1.4B Twin Eagle purchase.
counterthesis: These earnings are priced off natural gas: 9M realized price including derivatives was 3.54 per Mcfe and Q3 was 3.17, so a lower gas price compresses cash flow quickly, and 784M of 9M GAAP income came from derivative gains (464M in Q3), which are noncash mark to market in part. Twin Eagle adds a marketing business (marketing revenue 2.82B in nine months, margin thin) with 349M goodwill and 1,089M intangibles, and receivables and working capital swings inflate operating cash flow. Annualizing nine months is an approximation of a gas year with unusually strong first half pricing; the Q3 run rate (adjusted FCF 354M, adjusted EPS 1.46, about 5.84 annualized, about 14.5x) is much weaker. Hedge position, reserves, depletion and decline rates were not read. Capex guidance is about 3B with 11 to 12 rigs, so maintenance versus growth capex is not separated. Debt is 4.7B of senior notes from 2029 to 2035 plus 450M drawn on the credit facility.
invalidation: Henry Hub or Appalachia and Haynesville realized prices staying below about 3.00 per Mcfe for several quarters; free cash flow after dividends turning negative; net debt to EBITDAX above 1.5x; Twin Eagle impairment or marketing losses; reserve write-downs.
